balmoral--balmoral-anejo-xo.description: Royal Agio's Añejo XO carried the Balmoral Añejo line forward in 2015, after the 18-year-old wrapper of its predecessor ran out. Made in the Dominican Republic, it wraps a Brazilian leaf around a Dominican Olor binder and Brazilian, Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers. It smokes medium, with a cocoa sweetness up front giving way to earth and white pepper.

thirds.notes: Cocoa with a natural sweetness leads, earth and white pepper sit behind, and woody notes add depth.
Earth moves to the front with pepper close behind, while the cocoa sweetness drops away.
Earth stays dominant as white pepper rises, leaving mostly spice and only traces of cocoa.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Balmoral Añejo XO Rothschild Masivo review
Cigar Inspector – Balmoral Añejo XO Corona review

balmoral--balmoral-anejo-xo-oscuro.description: An extension of the Añejo XO announced in 2018, the Oscuro is rolled at Royal Agio's factory in San Pedro de Macorís, Dominican Republic. A stalk-cut Mexican San Andrés wrapper covers a Dominican Olor binder and filler of Nicaraguan Jalapa, Dominican Olor and stalk-cut Brazilian Mata Norte. Medium throughout, it centres on coffee, cedar and earth.

thirds.notes: Coffee bean, earth and white pepper open, then chocolate malt and cream join as cedar replaces the pepper.
Coffee grows and overshadows the malt and cream, with earth, a little citrus, cedar and returning pepper.
Cedar strengthens until it rivals the coffee, with earth, citrus and pepper still underneath.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Balmoral Añejo XO Oscuro Rothschild Masivo review

balmoral--balmoral-anejo-xo-nicaragua.description: Released in 2019, the Añejo XO Nicaragua is rolled at Royal Agio's own factory in San Pedro de Macorís, Dominican Republic, under a sun-grown Nicaraguan Habano wrapper. Brazilian Mata Norte in the filler brings an underlying natural sweetness. The maker describes oak, espresso, hazelnut and peppery spice, closing smooth and gently sweet.

balmoral--balmoral-serie-signaturas-duet.description: The first Balmoral Serie Signaturas release, Dueto was blended by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo Jr. with Royal Agio's Boris Wintermans and debuted in 2018. It is made at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic, with a Jalapa wrapper, an Estelí binder and filler of Nicaraguan and stalk-cut Brazilian Mata Norte tobacco. Pepper opens onto creamy chocolate, wood and fruit.

thirds.notes: Pepper leads over earth, then creamy chocolate, wood and a little fruit arrive, with spice and coffee cream.
Creamy chocolate and wood stay in front; fruit sweetness and spice return, with a citrus tang and a mineral touch.
Wood holds the front as earth arrives, and the finish turns dry and fruity while the chocolate recedes.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Balmoral Serie Signaturas Dueto Gran Toro review
Stogie Press – Balmoral Serie Signaturas Dueto review

balmoral--balmoral-serie-signaturas-paso.description: The second Serie Signaturas collaboration, unveiled in 2019, Paso Doble joins the blending styles of Royal Agio's Boris Wintermans and Litto Gomez of La Flor Dominicana. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and Ecuadorian Sumatra binder hold Dominican tobacco from the La Canela farms and stalk-cut Brazilian Mata Norte. Medium in strength and body, it leans on citrus, earth and pepper.

thirds.notes: Lemon zest, earth and black pepper open with cedar and a touch of nut; clove-like spice arrives late.
Pepper and a herbal lemon note lead over a dark molasses sweetness as the earth fades.
Nuts and cedar come forward with lingering lemon and a little more pepper, ending long with caramel sweetness.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Balmoral Serie Signaturas Paso Doble Gran Toro review
The Cigar Authority – Balmoral Paso Doble Robusto review

balmoral--balmoral-puro-nicaragua.description: A Nicaraguan puro in the Balmoral range, rolled in Nicaragua with wrapper and binder from Jalapa and filler from Ometepe, Estelí and Condega. It is full-bodied and robust yet controlled, opening with coffee and an oily, meaty richness before turning woody and roasted, and closing on green coffee and bark.

thirds.notes: Coffee and organic, earthy notes with a bready richness and an oily, meaty texture.
Woody, roasted tones take over, with a hint of black pepper at the base.
Meatier and a little more intense, with green coffee and bark carrying to the end.

sources.title: Cigars Connect – Balmoral Puro Nicaragua Rothschild Masivo

balmoral--balmoral-royal-selection-anejo.description: The predecessor of the Añejo XO, the Royal Selection Añejo 18 was named for its 18-year-old Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper and created by the brothers who run the family-owned Royal Agio. A Dominican Olor binder holds aged Nicaraguan ligero, Dominican Olor and Brazilian Bahia. It is woody and cocoa-toned, with spice and coffee building through the smoke.

thirds.notes: Cedar and cocoa lead, with cream and earth beneath and a light oak spice that builds gently.
Cedar and oak stay central as coffee, pepper and sweet spice join, with cocoa returning at moments.
Earth, coffee and charred wood dominate, with a savoury, meaty note and a spicy-sweet finish.
